item.description: arXiv:2611.14140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Davenport constant of a finite set of integer vectors is the maximum length of an irreducible zero-sum sequence over that set. For nonempty sets closed under negation, it equals the largest $\ell_1$-norm of a Graver basis element of the matrix formed by those vectors. We study extremal and average-case versions in growing dimension, with applications to integer programming. For integer cubes $[-R,R]^d \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ and the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^d$, totally unimodular encodings improve on the upper bounds from direct circuit decomposition, while random perturbations of Hadamard matrices give new lower bounds. A key ingredient is a uniform affine Bernoulli variant of Nguyen and Wood's surjectivity theorem. In every sufficiently large dimension the sign-cube lower bound is $d^{d/2}2^{-d-o(d)}$, and the integer-cube lower bound is $R^d d^{d/2}2^{-o(d)}$ uniformly for polynomially bounded integer radii. For random sign-cube sequences of even length conditioned on summing to zero, we prove a sharp threshold from irreducibility to reducibility at $d\log d/\log 4$, far below the extremal scale. For fixed $p$ and $R$, we determine exact exponential rates for lattice $\ell_p$-balls when $p=1$, $R\geq3$, or $2\leq p<\infty$, $\lfloor R^p\rfloor\geq3$. For each fixed integer $k\geq3$, we determine the exponential rate of the worst-case $\ell_1$-distance from an optimal LP vertex to the nearest integer optimum in standard-form programs with ternary matrices having at most $k$ nonzero entries per column.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Kuhlmann, Timm Oertel, Nicola Wengiel

item.title: Smoothed Least-Absolute Conditional Multidimensional Scaling via Iteratively Reweighted Majorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.14345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conditional multidimensional scaling combines latent coordinates with observed covariates to fit pairwise dissimilarities. We develop a smoothed l1 formulation using the shifted Charbonnier loss. We prove residualwise sharpness of the quadratic loss majorizer, monotonicity, compact containment, and stationarity of noncollapsed accumulation points. A uniform additive bound quantifies approximation to exact least-absolute conditional stress. The experiments use paired contamination, separately calibrated loss parameters, combined-configuration recovery, and direct checks of the theorem's inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Ling

item.title: Cotangent-lift inference of stochastic microbial dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the parameter estimation for the stochastic logistic and Lotka--Volterra diffusions from discrete, irregularly spaced observations corrupted by measurement noise, a setting typical of microbiome time series. For the logistic equation, the growth rate acts as a time change and does not enter the stationary law, so it can be identified only from the temporal structure of the data. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimator of the Euler scheme, with the observations taken as the states, coincides with the regression of log-increments on abundances used in the literature, and we characterise what this estimator cannot see under measurement noise: for the linearised dynamics, the law of consecutive pairs of observations is invariant along an explicit one-parameter family of relaxation rates and noise levels, and the regression converges to a limit set by the noise. Treating the true abundances as latent, we compute the likelihood with a Gaussian moment filter and show that measurement noise is precisely what couples the filter states across samples. The exact gradient is then the backward recursion of the discrete cotangent lift, whose cost, two to three likelihood evaluations, does not depend on the number of parameters, and we give the covector map of each filter step in closed form. In simulations, the latent estimator recovers the relaxation times, noise levels and interaction strengths that the regression biases, while larger communities require prior information on the interactions. In gut microbiome time series it attributes most of the variability of a dominant genus to measurement noise and estimates its relaxation time at about $64$ hours, with a large standard error.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e A. Capit\'an, Alberto Meg\'ias, Cristina Sard\'on

item.title: Parameter-free proximal bundle methods with adaptive stepsizes for hybrid convex composite optimization problems
item.description: arXiv:2410.20751v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a parameter-free adaptive proximal bundle method with two important features: 1) adaptive choice of variable prox stepsizes that "closely fits" the instance under consideration; and 2) adaptive criterion for making the occurrence of serious steps easier. Computational experiments show that our method performs substantially fewer consecutive null steps (i.e., a shorter cycle) while maintaining the number of serious steps under control. As a result, our method performs significantly less number of iterations than its counterparts based on a constant prox stepsize choice and a non-adaptive cycle termination criterion. Moreover, our method is very robust relative to the user-provided initial stepsize.
item.dc:creator: Renato D. C. Monteiro, Honghao Zhang

item.title: A definition of the background state of the atmosphere using optimal transport
item.description: arXiv:2504.11141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamics of atmospheric disturbances are often described in terms of displacements of air parcels relative to their locations in a notional background state. Modified Lagrangian Mean (MLM) states have been proposed by M.E.McIntyre using the Lagrangian conserved variables potential vorticity and potential temperature to label air masses in the instantaneous 3-D atmospheric state, and then rearranging air masses sandwiched between potential vorticity contours in potential temperature layers so that they are zonally symmetric. Methven and Berrisford used conservation of Kelvin's circulation to define the distribution of MLM state mass in zonal angular momentum ($z$) and potential temperature ($\theta$) coordinates given 3-D global data. We prove that for any such mass distribution in $(z, \theta)$ there exists a mapping to a unique mass distribution in geophysical coordinates (latitude and pressure) which minimises energy and completely defines the MLM state in a single hemisphere. Since the state is an energy minimum, it is suitable for quantification of finite amplitude disturbances and examining atmospheric instability. This state is obtained by solving a free surface problem, which we frame as the minimisation of an optimal transport cost over a class of source measures. The solution consists of a source measure, encoding surface pressure, and an optimal transport map, connecting the distribution of mass in geophysical coordinates to the known distribution of mass in $(z, \theta)$. We show that this problem reduces to an optimal transport problem with a known source measure, which has a numerically feasible discretisation, and we present a numerical solution using atmospheric reanalysis data. Additionally, our results hold for a large class of cost functions, and generalise analogous results on free surface variants of the semi-geostrophic equations.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Egan, John Methven, David P. Bourne, Mike J. P. Cullen

item.title: Regularized Extragradient Methods for Solving Equilibrium Problems on Hadamard Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2506.22391v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Employing two distinct types of regularization terms, we propose two regularized extragradient methods for solving equilibrium problems on Hadamard manifolds. The sequences generated by these extragradient algorithms converge to a solution of the equilibrium problem without requiring the Lipschitz continuity of the bifunction and without an upper bound on the regularization parameters. We establish convergence results for both algorithms under a monotonicity condition. When the bifunction is additionally strongly pseudomonotone, we derive global error bounds and establish $R$-linear convergence rates. Finally, we present numerical experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods.
item.dc:creator: Shikher Sharma, Pankaj Gautam, Simeon Reich

item.title: Policy Optimization in the Linear Quadratic Gaussian Problem: A Frequency Domain Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2508.17252v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) problem is a classic and widely studied model in optimal control, providing a fundamental framework for designing controllers for linear systems subject to process and observation noises. In recent years, researchers have increasingly focused on directly parameterizing dynamic controllers and optimizing the LQG cost over the resulting parameterized set. However, this parameterization typically gives rise to a highly non-convex optimization landscape for the resulting parameterized LQG problem. To our knowledge, there is currently no general method for certifying the global optimality of candidate controller parameters in this setting. In this work, we address these gaps with the following contributions. First, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the global optimality of stationary points in a parameterized LQG problem. This condition reduces the verification of optimality to a test of the controllability and observability for a novel, specially constructed transfer function, yielding a precise and computationally tractable certificate. Furthermore, our condition provides a rigorous explanation for why traditional parameterizations can lead to suboptimal stationary points. Second, we elevate the controller parameter space from conventional finite-dimensional settings to the infinite-dimensional $\mathcal{RH}_\infty$ space and develop a gradient-based algorithm in this setting, for which we provide a theoretical analysis establishing global convergence. Finally, representative numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical viability of the proposed approach. Additionally, the appendix section explores a data-driven extension to the model-free setting, where we outline a parameter estimation scheme and demonstrate its practical viability through numerical simulation.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Li, Xun Li, Yuan-Hua Ni, Xuebo Zhang

item.title: Differential Privacy for Euclidean Jordan Algebra with Applications to Private Symmetric Cone Programming
item.description: arXiv:2509.16915v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study differentially private mechanisms for functions whose outputs lie in a Euclidean Jordan algebra. Euclidean Jordan algebras capture many important mathematical structures and form the foundation of linear programming, second-order cone programming, and semidefinite programming. Our main contribution is a generic Gaussian mechanism for such functions, with sensitivity measured in $\ell_2$, $\ell_1$, and $\ell_\infty$ norms. Notably, this framework includes the important case where the function outputs are symmetric matrices, and sensitivity is measured in the Frobenius, nuclear, or spectral norm. We further derive private algorithms for solving symmetric cone programs under various settings, using a combination of the multiplicative weights update method and our generic Gaussian mechanism. As an application, we present differentially private algorithms for semidefinite programming, resolving a major open question posed by [Hsu, Roth, Roughgarden, and Ullman, ICALP 2014].
item.dc:creator: Zhao Song, Jianfei Xue, Lichen Zhang

item.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
item.description: arXiv:2510.18218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.
item.dc:creator: Luxuan Li, Xiao Wang, Chunfeng Cui

item.title: Zeroth-Order Gradient Estimators under Decision-Dependent Noise
item.description: arXiv:2510.24929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study zeroth-order optimization of a generally nonconvex optimization problem that is accessible only through a noisy black-box oracle, where the observation noise has zero mean and its distribution depends on the queried decision vector. Since the gradient of the objective function is inaccessible, various zeroth-order methods have been developed to solve the problem. However, it remains unclear how the choice of search directions affects the sample complexity of zeroth-order methods and how their algorithmic parameters should be selected. In this paper, we conduct a unified sample complexity analysis of zeroth-order methods across gradient estimators with different search directions. As a result, we show that gradient estimators that average over multiple directions, either uniformly from the unit sphere or from a Gaussian distribution, achieve the lowest sample complexity. The resulting sample-complexity bounds improve upon those of existing zeroth-order methods for nonconvex objective functions that are not bounded above. Moreover, through simulation experiments on multiple products pricing and strategic classification applications, we demonstrate the practical performance of zeroth-order methods with various gradient estimators.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Hikima, Akiko Takeda

item.title: Complexity of Projected Gradient Methods for Strongly Convex Optimization with H\"older Continuous Gradient Terms
item.description: arXiv:2602.07961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the complexity of projected gradient descent methods for a class of strongly convex constrained optimization problems where the objective function is expressed as a summation of $m$ component functions, each possessing a gradient that is H\"older continuous with an exponent $\alpha_i \in (0, 1]$. Under this formulation, the gradient of the objective function may fail to be globally H\"older continuous, thereby rendering existing complexity results inapplicable to this class of problems. Our theoretical analysis reveals that, in this setting, the complexity of projected gradient methods is determined by $\hat{\alpha} = \min_{i \in \{1, \dotsc, m\}} \alpha_i$. We first prove that, with an appropriately fixed stepsize, the complexity bound for finding an approximate minimizer with a distance to the true minimizer less than $\varepsilon$ is $O (\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \varepsilon^{2 (\hat{\alpha} - 1) / (1 + \hat{\alpha})})$, which extends the well-known complexity result for $\hat{\alpha} = 1$. Next we show that the complexity bound can be improved to $O (\log (\varepsilon^{-1}) \varepsilon^{2 (\hat{\alpha} - 1) / (1 + 3 \hat{\alpha})})$ if the stepsize is updated by the universal scheme. We illustrate our complexity results by numerical examples arising from elliptic equations with a non-Lipschitz term.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Chen, C. T. Kelley, Lei Wang

item.title: Discounted MPC and infinite-horizon optimal control under plant-model mismatch: Stability and suboptimality
item.description: arXiv:2604.08521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the robustness to plant-model mismatch of nonlinear systems in closed loop with (discounted) optimal controllers designed for a nominal model, with quadratic stage costs across finite and infinite horizons. By combining Lyapunov analysis with a unifying relaxed dynamic programming framework, we establish conditions that guarantee robust stability alongside improved suboptimality bounds compared to existing literature. A key step in our analysis is proving that stability counteracts time-accumulated error growth due to plant-model mismatch, yielding robustness bounds that hold uniformly across all prediction horizons.
item.dc:creator: Robert H. Moldenhauer, Karl Worthmann, Romain Postoyan, Dragan Ne\v{s}i\'c, Mathieu Granzotto

item.title: Nonlinear Stochastic Optimal Control and Optimal Stopping using the Fokker-Planck Transformation
item.description: arXiv:2604.12153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a theoretical framework for nonlinear stochastic optimal control problems with optimal stopping by establishing a density-based deterministic representation of the underlying diffusion. For state-independent diffusion, we rewrite the controlled Fokker-Planck equation as a continuity equation driven by a score-corrected velocity field, yielding a deterministic characteristic dynamics that reproduces the marginal law of the stochastic system. Leveraging Stein-type identities, we show that the associated distributional dynamic programming equation admits the same second-order differential operator as the distributional stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman formulation. Building on this representation, we formulate an optimal control problem with state-dependent terminal-time assignment and terminal distributional constraints and derive the first-order necessary conditions using variational analysis. We present the conditions both for a common terminal time and for the general case of state-dependent stopping.
item.dc:creator: Akan Selim, Siddhartha Ganguly, Ali Pakniyat, Panagiotis Tsiotras

item.title: Computing Lower Bounds on the Nonnegative Rank via Non-Convex Optimization Solvers
item.description: arXiv:2605.14058v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nonnegative rank of a nonnegative matrix $X$ is the smallest number of nonnegative rank-one factors that sum to $X$. Since computing the nonnegative rank is NP-hard, it is common to circumvent this issue by computing lower and upper bounds. In this paper, we propose non-convex formulations and practical implementations for four important lower bounds for the nonnegative rank, namely the fooling set bound (FSB), the rectangle covering bound (RCB), the hyperplane separation bound (HSB), and the self-scaled bound (SSB). In particular, to the best of our knowledge, our algorithm for computing the SSB is the first available in the literature. We compute the SSB for several matrices for which its value had not previously been reported. In some cases, the SSB provides the best known upper bound, while the other three bounds do not. Moreover, on canonical benchmarks, we show that our non-convex approaches are often competitive with existing methods. The paper also provides a consolidated reference for the current state of several classical lower bounds on a large number of benchmark matrices.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Baeckelant, Arnaud Vandaele, Nicolas Gillis

item.title: The parental parsimony problem on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.26919v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Phylogenetic reconstruction is one of the major challenges in computational biology. Among existing reconstruction methods for phylogenetic networks, an important subtask emerges in extending a leaf-labelling on a phylogenetic network to determine a most parsimonious tree inside the network. There exist different variants of this subtask depending on the biological model assumptions for which distinct evolutionary phenomena are captured by the network. In this article we assume that next to hybridization or recombination events, also allopolyploidy or incomplete lineage sorting are present. Then, finding the most parsimonious tree inside the network is called the parental parsimony score problem (PPS), a NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem. We provide the first constant-factor approximation for the PPS on arbitrary but fixed leaf labels and a class of networks on which the PPS remains NP-hard, namely binary, semi-simplex, tree-child phylogenetic networks. Furthermore, we introduce a novel exact solution algorithm for the PPS on binary, tree-child phylogenetic networks and analyze its performance on simulated data.
item.dc:creator: Martin Frohn

item.title: Data informativity for feedback rectification of switched linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.19578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For switched linear systems, we leverage the concept of data informativity for data-driven feedback rectification to design a stabilizing controller. The established rectified eigenstructure means that all closed-loop subsystems share a common set of eigenvectors and enables us to compute a common quadratic Lyapunov function to ensure global uniform exponential stability of the closed-loop system. The proposed methodology is illustrated for two examples including a model of an unmanned aerial vehicle.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Schmitz, Hannes Gernandt, Maria C. Honecker, Karl Worthmann

item.title: Fixed-time stabilization of systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of large unknown delays
item.description: arXiv:2607.24595v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study state-feedback fixed-time stabilization of continuous-time perturbed linear systems with nilpotent matrices in the presence of unknown large constant input/measurement delays with known bounds. By using an additional artificial delay, we design a feedback that for a precisely known linear system with a nilpotent matrix drives the state to zero in fixed time (which is larger than the bound of the unknown delay) and achieves input-to-state stability with a large exponential decay rate in the presence of additive disturbances and small system matrix perturbations and nonlinearities. For perturbed single integrators, fixed-time stabilization is achieved in the case of fast-varying unknown measurement delays with known bounds. The results are extended to discrete-time systems. Numerical simulations illustrate the efficiency of the results.
item.dc:creator: Kang-Kang Zhang, Emilia Fridman, Pengfei Wang

item.title: Unifying Variational View of Accelerated Primal-Dual Methods
item.description: arXiv:2609.09454v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a unifying variational framework for accelerated primal-dual flows in affinely constrained convex optimization. In particular, it is shown that applying the Euler-Lagrange-Rayleigh (ELR) principle to coupled augmented Bregman Lagrangians systematically generates accelerated dynamics over general Bregman geometries and recovers a family of existing primal-dual mirror and Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) flows as special cases. We then establish $\mathcal{O}(e^{-b_t})$ convergence guarantees for these flows under mild assumptions. Lastly, we show that the proposed framework for algorithmic development extends from finite-dimensional optimization to constrained optimization over probability distributions.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chang, Mehran Mesbahi

item.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
item.description: arXiv:2609.30438v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.
item.dc:creator: Cynthia Cheng, Xudong Chen

item.title: A Projection Anderson Acceleration Algorithm for Non-quasi-monotone Variational Inequalities with H\"older Continuous Terms
item.description: arXiv:2610.18370v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper proposes a Projection Anderson Acceleration (PAA) algorithm for variational inequality (VI) problems, where the underlying function is expressed as a finite sum of H\"older continuous functions and satisfies the $\sigma$-star strongly monotone condition that includes the star strong monotonicity with $\sigma = 1$ as a special case. In the absence of quasi-monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity, we establish the evaluation complexity of the PAA algorithm for finding an approximate solution. Specifically, for the star strongly monotone VI problems, the PAA algorithm needs at most $O (\log (\epsilon^{-1}) \epsilon^{2 (\underline{\alpha} - 1)})$ evaluations of the function and projection for finding an $\epsilon$-approximate solution, where $\underline{\alpha} \in (0, 1]$ is the smallest exponent of H{\"o}lder continuity of the component functions. We illustrate our theoretical results by numerical examples of non-quasi-monotone complementarity problems and non-monotone semilinear elliptic equations with non-Lipschitz terms.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Chen, C. T. Kelley, Lei Wang

item.title: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates
item.description: arXiv:2610.41927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiple local updates are widely used in decentralized optimization to enhance communication efficiency, often in conjunction with stochastic gradients when exact gradient computation is costly. However, such algorithms generally converge only to a neighborhood of the optimum, whose size depends on the stepsize and the variance of gradient noise. Variance reduction has been incorporated into ADMM-based methods to achieve exact convergence in expectation, but their stepsizes typically scale inversely with both the square root of the network size and the cube of the number of local updates, leading to slow convergence as the network size or the number of local updates increases. In this paper, we propose a novel primal-dual-based decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates variance reduction with multiple local updates, with a stepsize independent of the network size and inversely proportional to the number of local updates (rather than its cube), thereby enabling significantly larger stepsizes and faster convergence. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, we establish the first linear convergence guarantee in expectation for decentralized optimization with multiple local updates under stochastic gradients in the strongly convex setting. Beyond the theoretical guarantee, the proposed method exchanges only one variable per round, halving the communication cost compared with gradient-tracking-based methods. Numerical experiments further demonstrate its advantages in convergence speed and accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Jie Liu, Nicola Bastianello, Wenying Xu, Daniel W. C. Ho, Karl H. Johansson

item.title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.12502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Chambrion (IRMA, UNISTRA), Cristian Mendico (UBE, IMB)

item.title: Convex Minimization with Integer Minima in $\widetilde O(n^4)$ Time
item.description: arXiv:2304.03426v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a convex function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose set of minimizers is nonempty and closed, lies in a box of radius $R$ with $\log R\le\mathrm{poly}(n)$, and has integral extreme points, we give a randomized algorithm that finds an integral minimizer of $f$ with high probability using $O(n^2\log n+n\log R)$ calls to a separation oracle, $O(n+\log R/\log n)$ calls to an approximate shortest vector routine such as the LLL algorithm, and $O(n^4\log(nR)\log\log n)$ other arithmetic operations. The previous best polynomial time algorithm [Jiang, SODA 2021, JACM 2022] achieves $O(n(n\log\log n/\log n+\log R))$ oracle complexity, but its overall runtime is at least $\widetilde{\Omega}(n^8)$. We obtain our speedup by combining a variant of the volumetric center cutting plane method of [Vaidya, FOCS 1989], run on the hybrid barrier of [Lee, Sidford, Wong, FOCS 2015] with the fast implementation of [Jiang, Lee, Song, Wong, STOC 2020], and a variant of the LLL algorithm that reduces segments of consecutive basis vectors recursively. The method runs in blocks, so that shortest vectors are computed only $O(n+\log R/\log n)$ times, and each computation takes $O(n^3\log^3 n)$ arithmetic operations in exact arithmetic. For submodular function minimization, our result implies an algorithm using $O(n^3\log n)$ calls to an evaluation oracle and $O(n^4\log^3 n)$ arithmetic operations in total. Its oracle complexity is better than that of the algorithms of [Lee, Sidford, Wong, FOCS 2015] and [Dadush, V\'egh, Zambelli, SODA 2018, MOR 2021], which had the best running time before this work.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Jiang, Yin Tat Lee, Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang

item.title: The Star Geometry of Critic-Based Regularizer Learning
item.description: arXiv:2408.16852v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Variational regularization is a classical technique to solve statistical inference tasks and inverse problems, with modern data-driven approaches parameterizing regularizers via deep neural networks showcasing impressive empirical performance. Recent works along these lines learn task-dependent regularizers. This is done by integrating information about the measurements and ground-truth data in an unsupervised, critic-based loss function, where the regularizer attributes low values to likely data and high values to unlikely data. However, there is little theory about the structure of regularizers learned via this process and how it relates to the two data distributions. To make progress on this challenge, we initiate a study of optimizing critic-based loss functions to learn regularizers over a particular family of regularizers: gauges (or Minkowski functionals) of star-shaped bodies. This family contains regularizers that are commonly employed in practice and shares properties with regularizers parameterized by deep neural networks. We specifically investigate critic-based losses derived from variational representations of statistical distances between probability measures. By leveraging tools from star geometry and dual Brunn-Minkowski theory, we illustrate how these losses can be interpreted as dual mixed volumes that depend on the data distribution. This allows us to derive exact expressions for the optimal regularizer in certain cases. Finally, we identify which neural network architectures give rise to such star body gauges and when do such regularizers have favorable properties for optimization. More broadly, this work highlights how the tools of star geometry can aid in understanding the geometry of unsupervised regularizer learning.

item.title: Large Deviations Principle for Bures-Wasserstein Barycenters
item.description: arXiv:2409.11384v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the large deviations principle for empirical Bures-Wasserstein barycenters of independent, identically-distributed samples of covariance matrices and covariance operators. As an application, we explore some consequences of our results for the phenomenon of dimension-free concentration of measure for Bures-Wasserstein barycenters. Our theory reveals a novel notion of exponential tilting in the Bures-Wasserstein space, which, in analogy with Cram\'er's theorem in the Euclidean case, solves the relative entropy projection problem under a constraint on the barycenter. Notably, this method of proof is easy to adapt to other geometric settings of interest; with the same method, we obtain large deviations principles for empirical barycenters in Riemannian manifolds and the univariate Wasserstein space, and we obtain large deviations upper bounds for empirical barycenters in the general multivariate Wasserstein space. In fact, our results are the first known large deviations principles for Fr\'echet means in any non-linear metric space.
item.dc:creator: Adam Quinn Jaffe, Leonardo V. Santoro

item.title: Scheduling on identical machines with conflicts to minimize the total completion time
item.description: arXiv:2507.01759v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper addresses the problem of scheduling jobs on identical machines with conflict constraints, where certain jobs cannot be scheduled simultaneously on different machines. We focus on the case where conflicts can be represented by a simple undirected graph, and the objective is to minimize the total completion time. We establish that the problem is strongly NP-hard even on two machines with two distinct processing times. For unit-time jobs, we prove that the problem is polynomially solvable on two machines for any conflict graph, but becomes strongly NP-hard on three machines. We further identify polynomially solvable cases for specific classes of conflict graphs. For the general problem, we propose mathematical models, lower bounds, and a genetic algorithm. We evaluate their performance through computational experiments on a wide range of instances derived from well-known benchmark instances in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Nour ElHouda Tellache, Lydia Aoudia, Mourad Boudhar

item.title: The Phantom of Davis-Wielandt Shell: A Unified Perspective for Graphical Stability Analysis of MIMO LTI Systems
item.description: arXiv:2507.19918v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents a unified perspective based on Davis-Wielandt (DW) shell of linear subspaces for graphical stability analysis of multi-input and multi-output linear time-invariant feedback systems. Connections between DW shells and various graphical representations, as well as gain and phase measures, are established through an intuitive geometric perspective. We establish a strict DW separation theorem which characterizes subspace separation and provides a basis for comparing the implications and relative conservatism of graphical separation conditions. In particular, we introduce the rotated scaled relative graph ($\theta$-SRG) and show that its separation is equivalent to DW shell separation and is therefore the least conservative among all the graphical conditions considered. We derive pointwise and boundary stability conditions for bi-component feedback interconnections and establish a weak DW separation result that relaxes the strict separation requirement at open-loop poles. We also discuss applications to robust stability analysis and provide a numerical example illustrating how DW shells serve as a more reliable robustness indicator.
item.dc:creator: Ding Zhang, Xiaokan Yang, Axel Ringh, Li Qiu

item.title: Explicit MPC for the constrained zonotope case with low-rank matrix updates
item.description: arXiv:2511.02433v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solving the explicit Model Predictive Control (MPC) problem requires enumerating all critical regions and their associated feedback laws, a task that scales exponentially with the system dimension and the prediction horizon, as well. When the problem's constraints are boxes or zonotopes, the feasible domain admits a compact constrained-zonotope representation. Building on this insight, we exploit the geometric properties of the equivalent constrained-zonotope reformulation to accelerate the computation of the explicit solution. Specifically, we formulate the multi-parametric problem in the lifted generator space and solve it using second-order optimality conditions, employ low-rank matrix updates to reduce computation time, and introduce an analytic enumeration of candidate active sets that yields the explicit solution in tree form.
item.dc:creator: Stefan S. Mihai, Florin Stoican, Martin Monnigmann, Bogdan D. Ciubotaru

item.title: Configuration-Constrained Tube MPC for Periodic Operation
item.description: arXiv:2512.04239v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Periodic operation often emerges as the economically optimal mode in industrial processes subject to varying economic or environmental conditions. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control (MPC) framework for uncertain systems described by polytopic linear difference inclusions (LDIs), whose dynamics evolve as convex combinations of finitely many linear control systems subject to additive disturbances. The robust control problem is formulated as a convex optimization program over configuration-constrained polytopic tubes, with the objective of tracking a periodic tube that is optimal for a given economic criterion. Artificial variables embedded in the formulation ensure recursive feasibility and robust constraint satisfaction under changes in the economic criterion, and convergence to the optimal periodic tube when the criterion remains constant. To improve computational efficiency, we introduce a quadratic upper approximation of the periodic cost under a Lipschitz continuity assumption, yielding a Quadratic Program (QP) that preserves the above theoretical guarantees. The approach is demonstrated on an illustrative example and an eight-state ball--plate system.
item.dc:creator: Filippo Badalamenti, Jose A. Borja-Conde, Sampath Kumar Mulagaleti, Boris Houska, Alberto Bemporad, Mario Eduardo Villanueva

item.title: Adaptive Reparametrized Time for Score-Based Diffusion Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2607.02137v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study timestep allocation for score-based diffusion sampling, where a learned reverse-time dynamics is discretized on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted schedules are standard choices, but they rely on fixed prescriptions and can therefore be suboptimal. To address this limitation, we propose Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), a continuous-time control formulation that learns a time change by treating the speed of the sampling clock as the control, so that a uniform grid on the learned clock induces adaptive timesteps in the original diffusion time. Based on a leading-order Euler error surrogate, ART provides a principled objective for allocating timesteps along the sampling trajectory. To solve this deterministic control problem, we introduce ART-RL, an auxiliary randomized formulation with Gaussian policies that turns schedule learning into a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem. We prove that the randomized ART-RL formulation is equivalent to ART at the optimizer level, in the sense that its optimal Gaussian policy recovers the optimal ART time-warping rate through its mean. We further establish policy evaluation and policy improvement characterizations and derive trajectory-based moment identities that yield implementable actor--critic updates for learning the schedule. Across experiments ranging from controlled low-dimensional settings to image generation, ART-RL can be plugged into existing diffusion samplers by changing only the timestep grid, consistently improving sample quality over strong baseline schedules at matched budgets while leaving the rest of the sampling pipeline unchanged. The learned schedules also exhibit broad generalization, transferring without retraining across sampling budgets, datasets, solvers, pipelines, and representation spaces.
item.dc:creator: Yilie Huang, Wenpin Tang, Xun Yu Zhou

item.title: Adaptive stabilization of a leaderless bearing-constrained formation with disturbances
item.description: arXiv:2609.06355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of regulating and maintaining a target formation characterized by a set of bidirectional bearing constraints under disturbances. The agents in the formation are modeled by single integrators with deterministic bounded continuous disturbances of which both actual function and upper bound are unavailable for the control design. Due to the time-varying disturbances, the target formation is time-varying. We propose displacement/bearing-only based adaptive sliding mode control laws to uniformly asymptotically stabilize the time-varying target formation and reject the matched disturbances, and provide sufficient conditions to prevent possible collisions. A time-dependent adaptive design method is provided to convert the displacement-based control law to a bearing-only one. In addition, to alleviate chattering phenomena from sliding mode control, smooth adaptive control laws are introduced to guarantee uniform global boundedness of the desired formation. Finally, simulation results are given to support the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Minh Hoang Trinh, Chuong Van Nguyen, Quoc Van Tran, Tuynh Van Pham

item.title: Eigenvalues of the Hessian in Deep Learning: The Origin of Symmetry and Its Breaking
item.description: arXiv:2610.09919v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hessian spectra at trained models in deep learning exhibit a persistent pattern: eigenvalues organize into distinct clusters, including a large bulk near zero and a few isolated outliers. This paper shows that a natural account of these spectral phenomena emerges when the original setting is understood as a departure from a nearby, otherwise hidden, highly symmetric reference. Modifications, including changes to the architecture, data distribution, or parameter metric, expose a nearby reference configuration whose Hessian exhibits rich invariances-ones not accounted for by weight symmetries. There, symmetry enables a precise description of the spectra, forcing high-dimensional kernels and eigenvalues of large multiplicity. Returning to the original configuration breaks the Hessian symmetry and thereby produces the observed hierarchy of clusters and outliers. The framework is developed in some generality, with a detailed analysis of three-layer ReLU networks and applications to convolutional, graph, and transformer models, as well as to the NTK. The same mechanism is further shown to yield analogous spectral structures in layerwise Hessians and the Gauss-Newton matrix.
item.dc:creator: Yossi Arjevani

item.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.29914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Buffe, Alessandro Duca, Hugo Parada

item.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
item.description: arXiv:2611.03490v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions. A tuned robust predictor was also safe with synchronous switching, but not with per-rotor jitter.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Silano

item.title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
item.description: arXiv:2611.05726v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dantzig--Wolfe reformulation strengthens the linear relaxation of a mixed-integer program by convexifying constraint families, and each candidate costs a column generation run. The choice is hard when families strengthen the bound only together, as in classical lot-sizing, network-design, and facility-location formulations. We prove that when an evaluation convexifies at most $s$ of $k$ families, methods that observe only bounds need of order $k^w$ evaluations to find a hidden group of $w$ families in the worst case. A prediction missing $e$ members reduces this to $\Theta(k^e)$ through a staged search that need not know $e$. The orders extend to several groups, prices, and growing evaluation costs. We study two predictors: a lookahead at an optimal LP dual, which vanishes on groups whose families share no variable, and language models reading the model, verified by the staged search in JointDW. Such groups appear in three of ten MIPLIB-NL models whose bound can be improved and in all 59 benchmark instances. Given the coefficients of models with up to 16 families, one language model names a true group first in 249 of 252 answers. On the benchmark instances, decompositions chosen by language models from the text solve faster than those of GCG's detector.
item.dc:creator: Junbo Jacob Lian, Kaixuan Chen, Hanzhang Qin, Huiling Chen, Chaoyu Zhang, Chung-Piaw Teo

item.title: Predictive Neuromorphic Control of a Scanning Mirror System: An Event-Centric Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.11634v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Organizing control around events can reduce sensing and actuation demands while directly linking control decisions to the occurrence and timing of desired system behaviors. This paper proposes a novel event-centric model predictive control (MPC) framework that unifies event sensing, event prediction, and event regulation. Events define the feedback information, prediction horizon, and event-timing objectives, placing them at the center of predictive control design. The framework is developed for a scanning mirror system equipped with a baseline neuromorphic controller composed of spiking neurons that supports sparse actuation. The control objective is to achieve prescribed zero-crossing times and a desired scanning range while minimizing the mechanical energy transferred between the actuator and the mirror. A sampling-based algorithm is presented to obtain suboptimal solutions of the event-centric MPC optimization problem without requiring an explicit event-to-event prediction model. By grounding predictive optimization in events, the proposed framework opens a new direction for MPC design and its integration with neuromorphic control.
item.dc:creator: Changrui Liu, Robin Wroblowski, Anil Alan, Shengling Shi, Rodolphe Sepulchre, Bart De Schutter

item.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.12336v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.
item.dc:creator: Kala Agbo Bidi (XLIM, IDP), Thibault Liard (XLIM), Pierre Lissy (CERMICS UMR 9032)
